features.name: Cloud Migration Tooling
features.description: A tool for migrating on-premises Business Central databases to the cloud using SQL to SQL copy technology via Azure Data Factory. It provides automated company creation, data replication, data upgrade, and go-live capabilities with error detection and prevention.
caveats: Only supports upgrading to version 14 or later
Direct upgrade path from version 14 will be discontinued in April 2025 with version 26

features.name: Azure Data Factory Pipeline
features.description: Technology used to move data from on-premises SQL Server database to SaaS database as part of the cloud migration process. The setup wizard automatically creates the pipeline after providing the SQL connection string.
caveats: Requires integration runtime installation for on-premises SQL Server

features.name: Integration Runtime
features.description: Software component that must be downloaded and installed on the on-premises infrastructure to expose the on-premises SQL database to Azure Data Factory. Can be reconfigured using PowerShell to connect to different pipelines without reinstallation.

features.name: Self-hosted integration runtime
features.description: A self-hosted integration runtime is required for on-premises cloud migration setups, installed within the private network where the SQL Server database lives to securely pull and move data to the cloud.
caveats: not required if migrating from cloud-based SQL database

features.name: Automatic Company Creation
features.description: Feature that automatically creates companies in the cloud environment based on selections made in the setup wizard. Microsoft recommends doing this immediately after provisioning the tenant.
caveats: Company creation can take several hours for large numbers of companies

features.name: Data Replication
features.description: Process that copies selected tables from the on-premises database to the cloud. Progress can be tracked via refresh status, showing number of tables copied and successful transfers.
caveats: Only replicates necessary data according to Microsoft tables
Tables with no data are not reported in the count

features.name: Data Upgrade
features.description: Required step to upgrade the database schema after replication when migrating from older versions. Moves the tenant into maintenance mode, runs upgrade session exclusively, and includes automatic rollback capability if the upgrade fails.
caveats: Required as final step before completion
Tenant becomes inaccessible during upgrade
Automatic rollback available on failure

features.name: Cloud Migration Management Page
features.description: User interface page in Business Central for managing the cloud migration process. Allows users to track status, manage companies, invoke data replication, run data upgrade, and complete migration.

features.name: Direct upgrade path discontinuation from version 14
features.description: The direct upgrade and cloud migration path from Dynamics Business Central 14 will stop in April 2025 together with version 26, requiring intermediate upgrade steps due to removal of obsolete fields and tables.
caveats: affects versions before 25
requires upgrade to version 25 as intermediate step

features.name: Jump versions and five-version upgrade cycles
features.description: Starting with version 26, jump versions will be introduced where breaking SQL changes are made, and intermediate upgrade steps will be necessary every five versions (next jump version would be 30).
features.status_evidence_quote: we are planning to introduce these jump versions or to delete the objects every five versions so the next jump version would be 30
caveats: plan subject to feedback

features.name: SQL table definition alignment
features.description: Cloud migration requires aligning SQL table definitions between source and destination, including matching primary keys and field names/types exactly. Optional items like custom fields and table mappings can be handled through the UI.
caveats: different field lengths can be moved but names and types must match exactly

features.name: Table extension support for customizations
features.description: Cloud migration tooling can move customizations from main tables into table extensions through simple table mappings in the UI.

features.name: Three-character prefix/suffix field naming
features.description: Partners can introduce three-character prefixes or suffixes to field names through multiple options: C-side alignment with renames, SQL scripts, or data transfer objects for on-premises upgrades.

features.name: Invoke NV sanitized field commandlet
features.description: A PowerShell commandlet to eliminate non-printing characters from code fields before cloud migration, recommended to run on production database backups to clean up data corruption from years of operation.
caveats: should be run before cloud migration even if sanitization during migration is possible

features.name: Data Administration page
features.description: A page with ID 9035 containing data compression and archiving reports for data cleanup, available in all versions of BC and NAV to optimize the data set before upgrade and cloud migration.
caveats: page may not be available in navigation, reports exist in all BC and NAV versions

features.name: Cloud migration setup phase with preparation pipeline
features.description: The setup phase includes registration of integration runtime with Azure Data Factory, creation of a preparation pipeline that performs checks on both databases, and creation of stored procedures. A replication pipeline is prepared but not yet run.
caveats: stored procedures apply changes to on-premises database; recommended to test on backup first

features.name: Replication pipeline preparation
features.description: During setup, a replication pipeline is created with metadata about tables to be migrated and instructions for migration, ready to run but not yet executed.
caveats: Pipeline is not run during setup phase

features.name: Backup recommendation for on-premises migration
features.description: Cloud migration will apply changes to the on-premises database through stored procedures, so it is recommended to try cloud migration first on a backup of the production database.
caveats: Applies only to on-premises SQL migrations

features.name: Azure SQL database migration preference
features.description: Migrations from Azure SQL are more stable and faster than on-premises migrations, with improvements in replication of SQL variant fields and handling of large images, though Azure SQL incurs service charges.
caveats: Azure SQL requires service charges while database is online
Requires high compute and I/O tier

features.name: Postpone environment updates during cloud migration
features.description: Environment updates available in the admin center should be postponed to a later date to prevent interference with cloud migration, as running updates while cloud migration is enabled will forcefully stop the migration.
caveats: Failure to postpone results in forced cloud migration stop

features.name: Application Insights telemetry for cloud migration
features.description: Setting up Application Insights telemetry on the environment enables tracking of all flows involved in cloud migration, available from the admin center.
caveats: Optional but recommended

features.name: Table mappings for custom fields migration
features.description: Table mappings enable migration of custom fields from on-premises base tables to table extensions in SaaS, automatically handling data splitting across multiple extensions where field names and data types match.
caveats: Field names and data types must match exactly between on-premises and SaaS
On-premises fields must be renamed to match SaaS table extension prefixes
Only applicable to non-sensitive tables

features.name: Managed custom tables page for table mappings
features.description: A UI page called 'add table mappings' enables definition of migration table mappings with automatic parsing of table names from SQL, field filtering, and multi-select support for mapping to multiple table extensions.
caveats: Earlier inline table definition approach was error-prone

features.name: Table mappings export and import
features.description: Table mapping definitions can be exported as JSON files for later import, eliminating the need to re-enter definitions multiple times.

features.name: Programmatic table mappings via codeunit 401
features.description: Large partners with customized ISV solutions can automatically generate table mappings by subscribing to the on insert default table mappings event from codeunit 401 hybrid cloud management.
caveats: Primarily for large partners with customized ISV solutions

features.name: Selective table inclusion/exclusion in cloud migration
features.description: Ability to selectively include or exclude tables from cloud migration for non-sensitive tables that support page type extensions.
caveats: Only applies to non-sensitive tables
Details elaborated in separate 'what's new in cloud migration' session

features.name: Keep user permissions during cloud migration setup
features.description: Ability to disable the default behavior of removing user permissions when cloud migration is set up, allowing permissions to be retained throughout the migration process.
caveats: Optional; default behavior is still to remove permissions

features.name: Delegated admin consent for cloud migration
features.description: Delegated admins can perform cloud migration setup and actions after obtaining consent from a licensed super user, managed through a delegated admin consent page in the environment.
caveats: Requires consent from licensed user with super permissions
Consent can be revoked and migration will stop if revoked

features.name: Azure Data Factory pipelines for replication
features.description: Cloud migration uses Azure Data Factory pipelines to orchestrate data replication between on-premises and cloud environments, with Azure blob storage used as a staging area for data compression and optimization.

features.name: Large table vs bulk copy replication strategy
features.description: Large tables (exceeding 250 MB or 100,000 rows) are replicated individually, while smaller tables are compressed, chunked into JSON, and migrated together to a single staging table before being distributed to original tables in the cloud.

features.name: Incremental replication with SQL change tracking
features.description: After the initial full replication, subsequent replication runs use SQL change tracking to identify and migrate only the delta changes on-premises, enabling incremental updates without full re-migration.

features.name: Azure blob storage removal for Azure SQL
features.description: When replicating from Azure SQL databases, the staging step in Azure blob storage is no longer required, improving performance and reducing error risk.
caveats: Only applies to Azure SQL sources, not on-premise SQL Server

features.name: Cloud migration UI with status dashboard
features.description: New user interface displays overall replication status, successful and failed tables, company replication counts, and action history in a centralized dashboard.

features.name: Replication action log with run history
features.description: The UI displays a log of all replication actions performed, marking failed runs clearly for investigation and showing all replication attempts including successful retry runs.

features.name: Company replication filtering and selection
features.description: Users can filter the list of companies to identify which ones have not yet been replicated and manually select them for inclusion in subsequent replication runs.

features.name: Per-database table data review
features.description: A page allows filtering replicated data by company and database tables, with special handling for sensitive per-database tables that are delta-synced rather than replaced.
caveats: Cannot analyze internal or obsoleted tables
Tenant media table expected to show differences

features.name: Replication data filtering by table name
features.description: Users can search for and filter specific tables to check replication status and view configuration details such as whether a table is marked to replicate data.

features.name: Table inclusion-exclusion for replication
features.description: Functionality to include or exclude specific tables from replication, such as the change log table which was previously excluded by default.

features.name: Cloud migration completion and pause-abandon options
features.description: Users can complete the cloud migration to go live, or pause and abandon the migration with full recoverability of both states.
caveats: Both states are fully recoverable

features.name: 300 company limit in SaaS
features.description: SaaS environments enforce a hard limit of 300 companies for performance reasons, with a recommendation to stay around 250 to allow room for growth.
caveats: Recommended limit is 250 companies for growth headroom

features.name: Data storage capacity constraints
features.description: While there is no enforced data size limit, exceeding the default storage capacity blocks administrative operations like environment creation and copying, and requires additional storage purchase at go-live.
caveats: Exceeding quota prevents admin operations
Additional storage must be purchased at go-live

features.name: Upgrade as final step in migration
features.description: The upgrade step must be invoked as the absolute last step in cloud migration as it prevents additional replication or company additions afterward, otherwise requiring point-in-time restore or complete restart.
caveats: No additional replication or company moves allowed after upgrade

features.name: Per-database table upgrade constraints
features.description: During upgrade, per-database tables are upgraded and cannot accept additional pulls, preventing data corruption and requiring careful tracking of upgrade state.

features.name: Single-location data modification rule
features.description: During replication, users must not modify data in the SaaS database as changes may be overwritten or confuse the replication engine, so all changes should occur only in the on-premise system.

features.name: Upgrade process with versioning ignored
features.description: The upgrade invokes the regular upgrade flow while ignoring versioning, running all upgrade code units, placing the tenant in maintenance mode, and ensuring single-session access to prevent locks.

features.name: AppSource and custom app upgrade handling
features.description: Third-party and custom apps receive the same upgrade treatment as first-party apps with no special configuration needed, and their upgrade code is invoked automatically.

features.name: Sandbox testing before upgrade
features.description: Strong recommendation to test the upgrade in a separate sandbox environment after replication, allowing continued access to another instance if upgrade runs longer than expected.

features.name: Upgrade performance optimizations
features.description: Over 30 long-running upgrade methods have been optimized in recent versions, making upgrades to versions 21 or 22 faster than upgrades to version 19.

features.name: API upgrade background jobs
features.description: Functionality to run API upgrade as background jobs after cloud migration to pre-compute data and ensure fast APIs, can be safely run after migration instead of during it.
caveats: runs on large tables like customers items sales invoices
usually time consuming

features.name: User mapping functionality
features.description: Allows mapping of on-premises users to SaaS users through the defined user mappings page, updating username fields across tables used by business logic like items approvals and time sheets.
caveats: can only be run once per environment
must be done as last step

features.name: One-time user mapping execution
features.description: The user mapping step can only be run once per environment and should be performed as the last step before go-live.

features.name: Dataverse integration configuration
features.description: Post-migration configuration step to set up Dataverse integration and verify that API and data mappings are correct.

features.name: Multiple company migration in live tenants
features.description: Capability to move additional companies to SaaS in live tenants after initial go-live, though not officially supported and done at customer's own risk.
caveats: not officially supported
at customer's own risk
requires manual data fixes if errors occur
no support from Microsoft for patching data

features.name: Cloud migration troubleshooting documentation
features.description: Online resources documenting common errors that occur during cloud migration setup and replication phases, providing solutions for known issues.

features.name: Cloud migration telemetry events
features.description: Partner-facing telemetry events captured throughout the cloud migration process, including setup, replication, completion, and error events, available in documentation and telemetry tables.
caveats: requires telemetry to be enabled

features.name: Power BI cloud migration app
features.description: AppSource Power BI app with cloud migration tab that provides status overview of migrations across different environments, aggregated error views, KPIs, and log inspection without logging into the web client.

features.name: Telemetry-based alerts and notifications
features.description: Ability to set up alerts and email notifications or Teams notifications based on cloud migration telemetry events for proactive monitoring.
